name: Lithuania
snapshot: A NATO frontline state whose Social Democrat-led government fell in June 2026 when it dropped its populist partner, making party leader Mindaugas Sinkevičius prime minister.
culture: Lithuania was the last pagan country in Europe to convert to Christianity, in 1387, and once ruled a vast commonwealth with Poland. Basketball is close to a religion. The Hill of Crosses, covered with more than 100,000 crosses, symbolised resistance to Soviet rule. Lithuanian is one of the oldest living Indo-European languages.
society: Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence, in 1990. It has become a fintech hub, has stood up to China over Taiwan, and spends heavily on defence. Emigration has shrunk the population. Belarus has sent balloons carrying contraband across the border, forcing Vilnius airport to close repeatedly.
situation: The Social Democrats won the 2024 election. Prime Minister Gintautas Paluckas resigned in 2025 over business dealings and was succeeded by Inga Ruginienė, whose coalition included Nemunas Dawn, led by a politician on trial for antisemitic remarks. In June 2026 the Social Democrats ended that partnership, Ruginienė's cabinet resigned, and party leader Mindaugas Sinkevičius became prime minister on 14 July with the Union of Democrats "For Lithuania" as his partner.
power: A semi-presidential republic. The directly elected president leads foreign and defence policy; the prime minister leads the government with the confidence of the 141-seat Seimas.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius, since July 2026
